label: UGC NET June 2026 Paper 2 — Sampling Theory questions not in the 1–50 set (booklet numbers not known; identified by official question ID)

items.stem: If a stratified random sample of size 50 is to be selected by Neyman allocation from a population with N₁ = 150, N₂ = 350, S₁² = S₂² = 4, then the number of units to be selected from the second stratum is:
items.explanation: Idea: Neyman allocation takes nₕ proportional to NₕSₕ. When every stratum has the same standard deviation, this reduces to proportional allocation, nₕ ∝ Nₕ. Working: Neyman: nₕ ∝ NₕSₕ. With S₁ = S₂ this is proportional allocation: n₂ = 50 × 350/500 = 35. Official answer: C (35).

items.stem: Using Lahiri's method to draw a sample of size n with probabilities proportional to Xᵢ and with replacement, the probability of selecting the iᵗʰ unit (i = 1, 2, …, N) at any given draw is:
items.explanation: Idea: Lahiri's method is an accept/reject scheme that selects each unit with probability proportional to its size Xᵢ, exactly as cumulative-total PPS does, but without building cumulative totals. Working: Lahiri's method accepts unit i with probability proportional to Xᵢ, so P(unit i on a draw) = Xᵢ/ΣXⱼ = Xᵢ/(NX̄). Source note: The stem is printed as 'a sample of sign N'; read as 'a sample of size n'. Official answer: C (Xᵢ/(NX̄)).

items.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the different sampling methods: A. Simple random sampling with replacement is more efficient than simple random sampling without replacement. B. In the ratio method of estimation, the usual ratio estimator (ȳ_R) of the population mean (Ȳ) is a biased estimator. C. If the intraclass correlation between elements of a cluster is negative, the cluster sampling is more efficient than SRSWOR. D. If the intraclass correlation between units of a column is greater than −1/(kn−1), the systematic sampling is superior to simple random sampling. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Idea: judge each statement against a standard result: WOR versus WR, bias of the ratio estimator, the effect of the sign of the intraclass correlation in cluster sampling, and the efficiency condition for systematic sampling. Working: A false: SRSWOR is more efficient than SRSWR. B true: the ratio estimator is biased (bias O(1/n)). C true: with negative intraclass correlation cluster sampling beats SRSWOR. D false: systematic sampling beats SRS when the intraclass correlation is LESS than −1/(kn−1). Official answer: A (B and C only).

items.stem: Match LIST-I with LIST-II. LIST-I: A. Simple Random Sampling; B. Stratified Random Sampling; C. Cluster Sampling; D. Sampling with varying probabilities. LIST-II: I. To give due weightage to larger units; II. Sampling frame is not available; III. Homogeneous population; IV. Heterogeneous population.
items.explanation: Idea: link each method to the population situation it is designed for: homogeneous, heterogeneous (strata), no list of units (clusters), or units of very different sizes (PPS). Working: SRS suits a homogeneous population (III); stratification handles heterogeneity (IV); clusters are used when no list of elementary units exists (II); PPS gives larger units more weight (I). Official answer: D (A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I).
